title: PostHarvestPro: postharvest physiology and technology, quality, shelf life and sensory evaluation in the browser
description:
PostHarvestPro is a self-contained web application for postharvest research and teaching that follows the produce from harvest to the consumer entirely in the browser, with no installation, no third-party libraries and no server-side computation; the data never leave the computer. It computes quality and maturity indices (SSC/TA, BrimA, titratable acidity, moisture, firmness, weight loss, McKinney index, size grades) and CIELAB color (sRGB–CIELAB conversion, ΔE*ab, ΔE94 and ΔE00, citrus color, browning, whiteness, yellowness and tomato color indices). Deterioration kinetics of zero, first and second order are fitted by nonlinear least squares and compared by AIC, with the time to an acceptance limit and its delta-method interval; Arrhenius, Q10 and square-root (Ratkowsky) models give the shelf life at any temperature, accelerated shelf-life tests come with a prediction interval, and the time to rejection of each fruit is analyzed with right censoring by Kaplan–Meier (Greenwood), the log-rank test and Weibull, log-normal, log-logistic and exponential models. It also measures respiration and ethylene in static and flow-through systems, classifies the climacteric by an explicit rule, designs steady-state modified-atmosphere packages (with optional Michaelis–Menten respiration), and computes half and seven-eighths cooling times and the refrigeration load.

Losses along the value chain are summarized by stage in quantity and value with a Sankey diagram, Pareto critical points and a what-if simulation; mechanical damage is described by linear, quadratic, power and exponential curves and a logistic dose with Fieller's interval. The sensory block covers triangle, duo-trio, 2-AFC, 3-AFC and tetrad tests with Thurstonian d′, power and sample size, A–not A, paired preference, hedonic tests (analysis of variance, Tukey, Friedman), just-about-right penalty analysis, CATA (Cochran's Q, McNemar, correspondence analysis), descriptive profiles with panel performance and a principal-component product map, and serving plans with Williams designs and random three-digit codes. Postharvest trials are analyzed as treatment × time factorials (types I and III, Tukey–Kramer, LSD, Bonferroni and Dunnett) or as repeated measures (Greenhouse–Geisser, Huynh–Feldt, Mauchly), with comparison of slopes and a randomized field book. Packaging and cold-storage calculators give pallet and container loads, box vent area, psychrometrics with a chart, vapor-pressure deficit and water loss, storage cost and product compatibility. A last block writes a self-contained HTML report with the sections used, handling recommendations, methods, references and citation, printable to PDF, and saves the whole project as JSON. Figures export as SVG or PNG and tables as CSV or XLSX. The interface is in Spanish and English, with light and dark themes, and ten simulated example data sets (mango, chayote, coffee panel, tomato chain, avocado) let every block be tried without data of one's own.

Every engine was written from the published formula and compared against independent implementations in R 4.4.2, published tables or hand calculations, each comparison with its own tolerance: 443 tests and 71,199 comparisons, none failed, run both in the browser and in node. The archive includes the R reference scripts, the reference values and a report per area, the script that generates the simulated examples, and user manuals in Spanish and English (HTML and PDF).
